items.author: Ben (2026-09-08, on the cleared board); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: The phase 6 objective gains a reach-quality term, so a road tier is something it can see
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-08: "Roads should be visible in phase 6 too." The ruling is written into GENERATION_STRATEGY.md as the objective's FIFTH TERM; this item is the work.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT FORCED IT (archived NR-793, confirmed on a live ten-market world, seed ABCDEF01, every term alive):
  tier=1  IN_REACH=25658  raws=122  composite=0.010256174
  tier=3  IN_REACH=26024  raws=122  composite=0.010256174
The reach frontier moves by 366 tiles. Every scored term is bit-identical.

THE CAUSE IS ONE NUMBER, and it is raws_in_reach: 122 either side. A road tier scales traversal COST, continuously. Terms 1 and 4 read reach through a PER-RESOURCE COVERAGE BOOLEAN - is there any reachable deposit of resource R in this catchment - and that boolean is SATURATED. With 122 resource-market pairs already covered across 25,658 tiles, 366 more tiles introduce no pair that was not already covered. So the axis moves a continuous quantity the objective only reads through a threshold, and the search spends a third of every round proposing a change it cannot score.

THE CONSTRAINT, and it is the whole difficulty. Cheaper traversal everywhere is trivially better, so a reach-quality term entered as a FLAT VIABILITY BONUS would reward a uniformly well-connected map - precisely the evenness term 3 and GENERATION_STRATEGY.md § Asymmetry is the deliverable exist to prevent. The term must be a PER-MARKET reading whose SPREAD is scored, exactly like terms 1 and 2, never a single global number added to the composite.

SLICE 1 IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A FEATURE, and it decides what the term reads. Two candidates: the mean traversal cost from a market to the tiles in its catchment, and the in-reach tile COUNT rather than the coverage boolean. Both are continuous and both move when a tier does. Score candidates that differ ONLY in road tier and ask whether the chosen reading DISCRIMINATES between them at all. A reading that does not is not worth keeping, and that is an afternoon's answer rather than a wasted build. This is § The first slice is the scorer applied to the new term.

TWO THINGS TO CARRY, both from the archived phase 6 work. (1) The default-seed phase 6 fixture is a TWO-MARKET world on which balance and composite evaluate to zero for every candidate - it is not a sound basis for any phase 6 measurement, and NR-793's first reading was taken on it before being re-run on a live world. Use a 10-15 market world. (2) Adding a term changes every ranking and therefore the selected landscape, so this is a world-moving change and owes the digest discipline in DELIVERY.md § The digest re-bless is one act per WAVE.

DONE WHEN: road tier 1, 2 and 3 produce DIFFERENT composites on a 10-15 market world; the difference is reported per market rather than as one global number; an even-reach landscape does not beat an uneven one at the same mean; and the determinism of the argmax is unchanged across thread counts.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-08, on the visibility form: extra wizard rounds, leans per pass); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: Extend the world wizard from three rounds to five - the shell rounds 4 and 5 live in
items.design:
THE SCAFFOLD ITEM, and it is deliberately first: every other item in this sprint needs somewhere to draw.

wizard_round_count goes 3 -> 5 (src/core/app.hpp:384). The static_assert against ui::chain_round_count is the tell that the pip strip, the Back/Next chrome and the chart chain are all keyed to one constant - so the count is not a one-line change and the assert must be RE-EXPRESSED rather than deleted. The chain rounds stay THREE; the wizard rounds become FIVE, and the two constants stop being the same number.

WHAT ROUNDS 4 AND 5 SHOW IN THIS ITEM: a PLACEHOLDER each, honestly labelled. The globe already draws the real tile raster and keeps doing so; the round frame, the pip strip, Back/Next and the causal-reroll rule (rerolling 4 invalidates 5) all work end to end before any history is played back over them.

DONE WHEN: five rounds navigate live in the built app, Back from 5 lands on 4, and a capture exists for each new round.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-08, on the visibility form: extra wizard rounds, leans per pass); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: Round 4 - polity colour per region on the wizard globe, advanced across the history span
items.design:
WHAT BEN CHOSE TO WATCH (2026-09-08, visibility form): polity colours on the globe. Empires form, spread, stall at a strait and collapse in view.

THE THING THAT DOES NOT EXIST YET is the record it draws from. The sim carries the region table forward and hands the political map across at the epoch; it does not emit WHO HELD WHAT AT EACH STEP. That per-step ownership record is the actual work here, and it is a generation-layer change, not a UI one. Keep it small: a region-count-sized array of polity ids per recorded step, at a step granularity coarse enough that the record does not rival the world in size.

PASS 1 AND PASS 2 SHARE THE ROUND. They are one engine (GENERATION_STRATEGY.md, Three passes of simulated history); the boundary year is a MARK ON THE TIMELINE, never a screen break.

DETERMINISM: the record is an output of a deterministic sim and must not perturb it. Recording must not consume from the sim's stream.

DONE WHEN: a full span plays back on the globe in the built app, watched live, with the boundary year marked; and the same seed produces a bit-identical record twice.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-08, on the visibility form: extra wizard rounds, leans per pass); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: Leans per pass - named forces over the ancient and industrial spans, resolved against the seed
items.design:
BEN'S CALL (2026-09-08): yes, leans per pass - the wizard's preferences model extended past planetology.

THE MODEL IS UNCHANGED AND MUST STAY UNCHANGED: a lean is a NAMED LEAN on an axis, resolved against the seed by a resolve_* function, and no raw generated value is editable. It names a FORCE, never an outcome - the tune-the-forces-never-the-outcome rule is not relaxed for being player-facing, and 'guarantee me an empire' is exactly the reading it forbids.

WHAT THE AXES ARE IS THE DESIGN WORK OF THIS ITEM, and it is NOT settled. Each candidate axis must map onto a scalar the sim ALREADY reads, or it is a new mechanism wearing a lean's clothes. The obvious candidates to test: consolidation pressure (fractious vs consolidating) and sea legs (insular vs seafaring) for pass 1; industrialisation timing (late vs early) and tariff posture (open vs protective) for pass 2. A lean whose effect is not visible on the round's own globe is not worth offering.

DONE WHEN: each shipped axis moves a measurable outcome across a SEED SWEEP - not one seed - and none of them clamps.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-08, on the visibility form: extra wizard rounds, leans per pass); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: Round 5 - metros, reach across water, firm markers and charters, and the market carve
items.design:
FOUR OBJECTS, ALL FOUR CHOSEN BY BEN (2026-09-08), drawn in order on the epoch globe: metros growing out of the population centres the history grew and sacked; colonial reach across water; firm markers with their charters; the market carve and its price field.

THIS ROUND SHOWS THE SELECTED LANDSCAPE, NOT THE SEARCH. Phase 6 scores candidates statically in milliseconds; a ranking is not a spectacle. The player watches the winner being drawn.

PLACEHOLDERS ARE EXPECTED AND ARE THE POINT. Phase 6's search is not built (BL-770 was cancelled with the board clear) and colonial ties do not cross the handoff yet. Each of the four draws from whatever is real today - centres, corporations and markets all are; reach across water is the one with nothing behind it - and is LABELLED as a placeholder where it is one. An unlabelled placeholder is a lie the next session will believe.

THIS PAYS THREE OF THE FOUR OWED VISIBILITY ITEMS: the region surface, the market-carving explanation, and background firms - the last of which stops being blocked by the worker-thread objection, because a wizard round is not the worker's loading screen.

DONE WHEN: all four draw in the built app on a LIVE click-through, each placeholder is visibly marked as one, and the Visibility table's verdicts are updated to match what actually renders.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-08, on the visibility form: extra wizard rounds, leans per pass); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: The wait becomes the round - run the real pass inside rounds 4 and 5, drawing as it computes
items.design:
THE STRUCTURAL PROBLEM THIS ITEM EXISTS FOR. The planetology rounds re-run their chain as a pure throwaway preview on EVERY control move. The history sim is the most expensive pass in the project and cannot be previewed that way at any budget - so rounds 4 and 5 invert the wizard's own mechanism, and that inversion needs stating rather than discovering.

THE SHAPE: the player sets the leans, presses Run, and the pass runs INSIDE the round with its output drawn as it computes. Accept moves on; reroll runs it again. The generation_progress sink already exists for the loading screen and is the natural feed; what changes is that generation stops being one call behind a bar and becomes calls the player initiates.

BEN'S RULING THAT LICENSES IT (2026-09-08): 'a watched wait needs no budget' - which is why the whole startup-budget chain was dropped rather than deferred.

AND THE OBLIGATION THAT REPLACES THE BUDGET IS SHARPER, NOT LOOSER. A watched wait must be WORTH WATCHING. A round that shows a still globe for ninety seconds is worse than the bar it replaced, because the bar at least admitted it was a wait. If the playback has dead stretches, the answer is to make them move - never to hide them behind a caption.

START_NEW_GAME IS THE SEAM THAT MOVES. The one-and-only generation call splits, and the clock rebase at handoff must still hold: wall time spent watching must not land as elapsed in-game days.

DONE WHEN: a live click-through from the menu to play, timed, with no stretch longer than a few seconds in which nothing on the globe changes.
